config.title: Build typed backoff strategy interface

intro.title: Build typed backoff strategy interface
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed TypeScript interface for a backoff strategy, which is a common pattern for handling retries in network requests or operations that may fail. You will learn how to define a contract using TypeScript interfaces to specify the structure and types for backoff properties like delay and max attempts. The core concept involves using TypeScript's interface system to enforce type safety and ensure your strategy objects have the correct shape. You'll work with basic TypeScript constructs like interfaces, optional properties, and number types to create a reusable and reliable backoff strategy definition.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, typed backoff strategies are essential for handling API rate limiting and network instability in production systems. For example, when a dashboard fetches analytics data from a third-party service like Stripe or GitHub API, exponential backoff with jitter prevents overwhelming their servers during temporary outages. E-commerce platforms use typed backoff interfaces when retrying payment processing after declined transactions, ensuring type-safe configuration of delay intervals and maximum attempts. This pattern also appears in mobile apps that synchronize data with cloud services, where developers need compile-time guarantees about retry logic parameters to prevent runtime errors during intermittent connectivity.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript interface that defines the structure of a backoff strategy
Implement a concrete class that satisfies the backoff strategy interface
Apply type annotations to enforce proper return types for backoff calculation methods
Configure interface properties to control delay behavior and retry limits
Initialize a backoff strategy instance with specific configuration values
Manipulate the backoff state to calculate progressive delay intervals
Integrate the typed backoff strategy into a simulated retry mechanism

steps.title: Define the BackoffStrategy interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'BackoffStrategy' with a method signature 'calculateDelay' that takes a number parameter 'attempt' and returns a number.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the method signature inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a TypeScript interface that defines the structure for a backoff strategy with a method to calculate delays.
successCriteria: The BackoffStrategy interface is defined with a calculateDelay method that accepts a number parameter and returns a number.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the calculateDelay method has the correct parameter type and return type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition doesn't match the requirements. Check that you used the 'interface' keyword, named it 'BackoffStrategy', and included the calculateDelay method with proper types.

steps.instruction: Inside the BackoffStrategy interface, add a method signature called calculateDelay that takes a parameter named attempt of type number and returns a number.
steps.hint: Add a method signature like calculateDelay(attempt: number): number; inside the interface body.
steps.expectedOutcome: The BackoffStrategy interface now includes a calculateDelay method signature that defines the contract all backoff strategies must follow.
successCriteria: The interface has a method calculateDelay(attempt: number): number;

steps.title: Implement calculateDelay in LinearBackoff
steps.instruction: Inside the LinearBackoff class, implement the calculateDelay method to return the baseDelay multiplied by the attempt number.
steps.hint: The method should take an attempt number parameter and return a number. Multiply this.baseDelay by the attempt parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The LinearBackoff class will have a working calculateDelay method that computes the delay based on the attempt number.
successCriteria: The calculateDelay method is implemented in LinearBackoff and returns baseDelay * attempt.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.hint: Start with 'class ExponentialBackoff implements BackoffStrategy { }' and leave the implementation details for later steps.

steps.title: Add constructor to ExponentialBackoff
steps.instruction: Add a constructor to the ExponentialBackoff class that accepts a baseDelay parameter (type number) and an optional factor parameter (type number) with a default value of 2.
steps.hint: Remember to use the constructor keyword and assign the parameters to instance properties. The factor parameter should have a default value in the parameter list.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ExponentialBackoff class will have a constructor that initializes instance properties for baseDelay and factor.
successCriteria: ExponentialBackoff has a constructor with baseDelay (number) and factor (number, default 2) parameters, and assigns them to instance properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Implement calculateDelay in ExponentialBackoff
steps.instruction: Inside the ExponentialBackoff class, implement the calculateDelay method to return baseDelay multiplied by factor raised to the power of (attempt-1).
steps.hint: Use Math.pow(factor, attempt-1) to calculate the exponential factor, then multiply it by baseDelay. Remember to return the result.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ExponentialBackoff class will have a working calculateDelay method that computes exponential backoff delays.
successCriteria: The calculateDelay method returns baseDelay * Math.pow(factor, attempt-1) with proper TypeScript syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: The calculateDelay method isn't implemented correctly. Review the exponential backoff formula: baseDelay × factor^(attempt-1).
